outcome: Servers arrive at every site already built to a proven specification, keeping a multi-site launch on schedule.
overview: A cloud-telephony provider in India had to deliver, configure and bring live forty-two Dell PowerEdge rack servers across several locations inside a tight go-live window. Redington ran it as a phased batch deployment, with system, RAID and application configuration performed at staging per batch rather than per server on arrival at site. The work is logistics as much as engineering, and that is the point of keeping this record: the common failure in a multi-site deployment is not the technology, it is discovering at site three that the build was never actually repeatable.

benefits.text: Servers are built to a repeatable configuration in batches rather than individually on arrival
benefits.limits: The published reference describes one named customer engagement. It is evidence that Redington has delivered this, and it is not a performance figure that transfers to the next customer

benefits.text: Multi-site delivery is sequenced so a fixed go-live date can be planned against
benefits.limits: Sequencing depends on site readiness that the customer controls; a site not ready to receive equipment stops its batch

benefits.text: Commodity server hardware keeps the estate portable to another vendor at the next refresh
benefits.limits: Sized from measured capacity and performance data; a design built on invoice history or on projected growth alone produces a quotation rather than an architecture

residency: Servers and their data remain at the customer’s own sites

notFor.situation: A single-site deployment of a handful of servers
notFor.why: Batch build and staging logistics exist to serve multi-site scale

notFor.situation: A workload requiring engineered converged infrastructure
notFor.why: Commodity rack servers serve a different design point

scope:
Model: Redington solutions engineering and logistics with an accredited Dell implementation partner; the referenced engagement was delivered directly by Redington · Duration: Driven by the customer’s go-live date and site readiness rather than by build effort
Support model: Vendor hardware support with a replacement term matched to service criticality; Redington coordinates the vendor case and holds the deployment relationship.
1) Specify — build specification agreed covering system, storage and application prerequisites
2) Stage — first batch built and verified against the specification before shipment
3) Deliver — batches sequenced against confirmed site readiness
4) Commission and hand over — sites commissioned to go-live, operations handed over
deliverables: Every unit is verified against the frozen specification before it leaves staging
Site readiness is confirmed in writing before each batch ships
Commissioning at each site completes without a build defect traced to staging
effort: Driven by the customer’s go-live date and site readiness rather than by build effort
